outline.chapter_title: Introduction to RL for Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by explaining the role of Reinforcement Learning (RL) in scaling the reasoning capabilities of LLMs and reviewing the foundational algorithms that lead up to GSPO.
subtopics: The role of RL in LLM scaling (e.g., reasoning, math, and programming)
Review of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)
The computational burden of Value Models in PPO
Introduction to Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
The core mechanism of group-based advantage estimation

outline.chapter_title: The Theoretical Flaws of Token-Level Importance Sampling
outline.description: This chapter explores the mathematical and practical reasons why token-level importance weights in algorithms like GRPO lead to instability and model collapse.
subtopics: Foundations of Importance Sampling: Target vs. Behavior distributions
The 'Ill-Posed' nature of GRPO's objective
Token-level vs. Sequence-level weights: The variance problem
The impact of response length on gradient noise
Understanding catastrophic model collapse in large-scale RL

outline.description: This chapter introduces the GSPO algorithm, detailing its objective function, the definition of the sequence-level importance ratio, and the logic behind its design.
subtopics: The GSPO objective function
Defining the sequence-level importance ratio ($s_i$)
The necessity of length normalization in sequence likelihoods
Sequence-level clipping: Aligning reward units with optimization units
Comparison of clipping ranges between GSPO and GRPO

outline.description: A deep dive into the calculus behind GSPO to understand how it differs from GRPO at the gradient level, and an exploration of the GSPO-token variant for finer control.
subtopics: Deriving the gradient of the GSPO objective
Comparative analysis: How GSPO vs. GRPO weight token log-likelihoods
The stability benefit of equal token weighting
GSPO-token: Enabling token-wise advantage customization
Mathematical equivalence between GSPO and GSPO-token under uniform advantages

outline.description: This chapter explains the unique challenges of training sparse MoE models with RL and how GSPO inherently solves these issues without needing complex auxiliary strategies.
subtopics: Sparse activation and expert-activation volatility
Why token-level importance ratios fail in MoE architectures
The 'Routing Replay' strategy: Background and limitations
How GSPO's sequence-level focus bypasses routing instability
Benefits of removing artificial routing constraints on model capacity

outline.description: The final chapter examines the experimental results of GSPO, analyzes the counter-intuitive nature of its clipping behavior, and discusses its impact on RL system architecture.
subtopics: Performance benchmarks: AIME, LiveCodeBench, and CodeForces
Analysis of training efficiency and compute scaling
The paradox of clipping fractions: Why more clipping can lead to better efficiency
Precision discrepancies between training and inference engines
Simplifying RL infrastructure through sequence-level likelihoods
